78615-the-tide.title: The Tide
78615-the-tide.creator: Unknown
78615-the-tide.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. She felt very young and invincible as she stood there with her back to the window. She had asked to be alone because she was afraid of the exuberance that had taken possession of her on the way back from the cemetery. Everything had looked so fresh, so gay, so desirable--streets, houses, little flocks of sparrows, people passing with disinterested glances at the long procession of funeral hacks.

arxiv-2102-06900.title: Segmenting two-dimensional structures with strided tensor networks
arxiv-2102-06900.creator: Raghavendra Selvan, Erik B Dam, Jens Petersen
arxiv-2102-06900.description: Abstract Tensor networks provide an efficient approximation of operations involving high dimensional tensors and have been extensively used in modelling quantum many-body systems. More recently, supervised learning has been attempted with tensor networks, primarily focused on tasks such as image classification.

arxiv-2104-02555.title: Fourier Image Transformer
arxiv-2104-02555.creator: Tim-Oliver Buchholz, Florian Jug
arxiv-2104-02555.description: Abstract Transformer architectures show spectacular performance on NLP tasks and have recently also been used for tasks such as image completion or image classification. Here we propose to use a sequential image representation, where each prefix of the complete sequence describes the whole image at reduced resolution.

arxiv-2108-12525.title: Field induced conducting state in Mott insulator
arxiv-2108-12525.creator: X. Z. Zhang, Z. Song
arxiv-2108-12525.description: Abstract Electron–electron repulsion, on the one hand, can result in bound pair, which has heavy effective mass. On the other hand, it is also the cause of Mott insulator. We study the effect of a staggered magnetic field on a Hubbard model.

arxiv-2112-10045.title: p p -wave superconductivity in Luttinger semimetals
arxiv-2112-10045.creator: Julia M. Link and Igor F. Herbut
arxiv-2112-10045.description: Abstract We consider the three-dimensional spin-orbit-coupled Luttinger semimetal of “spin” 3 / 2 3/2 particles in presence of weak attractive interaction in the l = 1 l=1 ( p p -wave) channel, and determine the low-temperature phase diagram for both particle- and hole dopings.

arxiv-2202-03258.title: Enhanced Higgs pair production from higgsino decay at the HL-LHC
arxiv-2202-03258.creator: Jianpeng Dai, Tao Liu, Daohan Wang, Jin Min Yang
arxiv-2202-03258.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Jianpeng Dai, Tao Liu, Daohan Wang, Jin Min Yang. The scenario of multi-sector SUSY breaking predicts pseudo-goldstinos which are not absorbed by the gravitino and their mass can be as low as 𝒪 ⁡ ( 0.1 ) {{\cal O}(0.1)} GeV.

arxiv-2206-03575.title: Certifying Data-Bias Robustness in Linear Regression
arxiv-2206-03575.creator: Anna P. Meyer, Aws Albarghouthi, Loris D’Antoni
arxiv-2206-03575.description: Abstract Datasets typically contain inaccuracies due to human error and societal biases, and these inaccuracies can affect the outcomes of models trained on such datasets. We present a technique for certifying whether linear regression models are pointwise-robust to label bias in the training dataset, i.e.

arxiv-2402-16900.title: The time-fractional heat equation driven by fractional time-space white noise
arxiv-2402-16900.creator: Rahma Yasmina Moulay Hachemi & Bernt Øksendal
arxiv-2402-16900.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Rahma Yasmina Moulay Hachemi & Bernt Øksendal. We give an introduction to the time-fractional stochastic heat equation driven by 1+d-parameter fractional time-space white noise, in the following two cases: (i) With additive noise (ii) With multiplicative noise.

arxiv-2404-13853.title: ICST-DNET: An Interpretable Causal Spatio-Temporal Diffusion Network for Traffic Speed Prediction Thanks: Y. Rong, Y. Mao, and L. Chen are with the College of Computer and Software, Hohai University, Nanjing 210098, China (e-mail: rongyi1220@163.com; yingchimao@hhu.edu.cn; 221307050018@hhu.edu.cn) T
arxiv-2404-13853.creator: Yi Rong, Yingchi Mao, Yinqiu Liu, Ling Chen, Xiaoming He
arxiv-2404-13853.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yi Rong, Yingchi Mao, Yinqiu Liu, Ling Chen, Xiaoming He. Traffic speed prediction is significant for intelligent navigation and congestion alleviation. However, making accurate predictions is challenging due to three factors: 1) traffic diffusion, i.e., the spatial and temporal causality existing between the traffic conditions of multiple neighboring roads, 2) the poor interpretability of traffic data with complicated spatio-temporal correlations, and 3) the latent pattern of traffic speed fluctuations over time, such as morning and evening rush.

arxiv-2504-07219.title: Be X-ray binary pulsar SXP 138: non-linear spin-down, pulse and spectral characteristics
arxiv-2504-07219.creator: Soham Pravin Sanyashiv, Sayantan Bhattacharya, Sudip Bhattacharyya
arxiv-2504-07219.description: Abstract We study the timing and spectral properties of the Be/X-ray binary pulsar SXP 138 using four NuSTAR observations spanning 2016 to 2017. Analysis of the light curves using the Lomb-Scargle periodogram shows an increase in the spin period of SXP 138 from 140.69 to 140.85 seconds, indicating that the source is in the propeller regime.

arxiv-2509-12894.title: DialNav: Multi-turn Dialog Navigation with a Remote Guide
arxiv-2509-12894.creator: Leekyeung Han, Hyunji Min, Gyeom Hwangbo, Jonghyun Choi, Paul Hongsuck Seo
arxiv-2509-12894.description: Abstract We introduce DialNav, a novel collaborative embodied dialog task, where a navigation agent (Navigator) and a remote guide (Guide) engage in multi-turn dialog to reach a goal location. Unlike prior work, DialNav aims for holistic evaluation and requires the Guide to infer the Navigator’s location, making communication essential for task success.

arxiv-2510-09045.title: LLM Based Long Code Translation using Identifier Replacement
arxiv-2510-09045.creator: Manojit Chakraborty, Madhusudan Ghosh, Rishabh Gupta
arxiv-2510-09045.description: Abstract In the domain of software development, LLMs have been utilized to automate tasks such as code translation, where source code from one programming language is translated to another while preserving its functionality. However, LLMs often struggle with long source codes that don’t fit into the context window, which produces inaccurate translations.

arxiv-2510-19480.title: Online Two-Stage Submodular Maximization
arxiv-2510-19480.creator: Iasonas Nikolaou, Miltiadis Stouras, Stratis Ioannidis, Evimaria Terzi
arxiv-2510-19480.description: Abstract Given a collection of monotone submodular functions, the goal of Two-Stage Submodular Maximization ( 2SSM ) ( Balkanski et al. 2016 ) is to restrict the ground set so an objective selected u.a.r. from the collection attains a high maximal value, on average, when optimized over the restricted ground set.

arxiv-2510-22657.title: Synthesis of State-Attack Strategies for Anonymity and Opacity Violation in Discrete Event Systems
arxiv-2510-22657.creator: Xiaoyan Li, Christoforos N. Hadjicostis
arxiv-2510-22657.description: Abstract Attacks, including the manipulation of sensor readings and the modification of actuator commands, pose a significant challenge to the security and privacy of automated systems. This paper considers discrete event systems that can be modeled with nondeterministic finite state automata that are susceptible to state attacks.

britannica-1911-pastoral-staff.title: Pastoral Staff (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-pastoral-staff.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-pastoral-staff.description: Article 'Pastoral Staff' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 20), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. It is some five feet long, ending at the top in a crook (volute) bent inwards, and made of metal, ivory or wood. If of metal, it is hollow; if of wood, it is usually covered with metal. The crook is usually richly ornamented, and is divided from the shaft by a boss; the shaft is commonly separated into sections by rings, so that it can be taken to pieces.

pmc-10647234.title: Single Line-to-Ground Fault Type Multilevel Classification in Distribution Network Using Realistic Recorded Waveform
pmc-10647234.creator: Jiajun Liu, Chenjing Li, Yue Liu, Ji Sun, Haokun Lin
pmc-10647234.description: The further identification of fault types for single line-to-ground faults (SLGFs) in distribution networks is conducive to determining the cause of grounding faults and formulating targeted measures for hidden danger treatment and fault prevention. For the six types of SLGFs generated in the actual power grid, this paper deeply studies their fault characteristics.

pmc-11337712.title: Exploring the MAPPING application to facilitate risk communication and shared decision-making between physicians and patients with gynaecological cancer
pmc-11337712.creator: Mijra Koning, Christianne Lok, Dirk T Ubbink, Johanna Wilhelmina Maria Aarts
pmc-11337712.description: This is an observational study in which we evaluated current levels of risk communication (RC) among gynaecological oncologists and their view on the Mapping All Patient Probabilities in Numerical Graphs (MAPPING) application as a possible tool to facilitate RC and shared decision-making (SDM). In part A, we audio-recorded 29 conversations between gynaecological oncologists and patients when discussing treatment options.

pmc-11619984.title: Barley a nutritional powerhouse for gut health and chronic disease defense
pmc-11619984.creator: Arif Ali, Zakir Ullah, Rehman Ullah, Mohsin Kazi
pmc-11619984.description: BackgroundDigestive issues are recognized as significant contributors to various chronic diseases, including obesity, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease. Barley, a traditional grain, offers considerable promise in addressing these health challenges due to unique nutritional and bioactive compounds.ObjectiveThis review examines the therapeutic potential of various parts of barley, underutilized resource, for chronic disease prevention and management.

pmc-12606455.title: The Atrioventricular and Ventriculo-arterial Junctions: A Clinical Perspective for Electrophysiological and Structural Intervention. Part 1: The Atrioventricular Junctions
pmc-12606455.creator: Robert H Anderson, Damian Sanchez-Quintana, Diane E Spicer, Justin T Tretter, Demosthenes G Katritsis
pmc-12606455.description: An in-depth knowledge of the anatomy of the atrioventricular and ventriculo-arterial junctions of the heart is necessary for the safe implementation of transcatheter approaches for electrophysiological and structural intervention. In the first part of this review, the atrioventricular junctional areas are revisited from the perspective of their anatomy.

pmc-12711935.title: Psychological and Related Factors Influencing Adherence to Biologic Therapies in Asthma: A Scoping Review
pmc-12711935.creator: Valentina Poletti, Eleonora Volpato
pmc-12711935.description: Purpose of ReviewThis scoping review aimed to explore psychological and related biopsychosocial factors influencing adherence to biologic therapies among individuals with asthma. Despite the proven efficacy of biologics for severe type 2 inflammation, real-world adherence remains variable. The review sought to identify individual, clinical, and contextual determinants that facilitate or hinder adherence behaviors.

pmc-13008692.title: Antineuronal antibody titres in autoimmune encephalitis: clinical implications for diagnosis and long-term immunotherapy
pmc-13008692.creator: Hanna Schwab, Josua Kegele, Markus C. Kowarik, Holger Lerche, Stephan Lauxmann
pmc-13008692.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionThe role of antineuronal antibody titres in the acute and long-term diagnostic and therapeutic management of autoimmune encephalitis (AE) remains unclear. In this retrospective monocentric cohort study, we aimed to (I) identify specific characteristics in antibody testing distinguishing AE from non-AE patients, (II) evaluate the prognostic significance of antineuronal antibody findings and (III) assess outcomes and long-term immunotherapy in patients with AE.MethodsPatients with suspected autoimmune-associated neuropsychiatric conditions underwent antineuronal antibody testing between 01/2017 and 03/2023.

pmc-13049329.title: Recurrent aquaporin 4-immunoglobulin G-positive neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder in a patient with long-standing rheumatoid arthritis: A case report
pmc-13049329.creator: Xuechun Jiang, Jinghua Chen, Ying Wen, Lei Yuan, Jinfeng Zhang
pmc-13049329.description: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder is an autoimmune astrocytopathy that primarily affects the optic nerves and spinal cord. Its association with rheumatoid arthritis is remarkably rare, with only 15 documented cases reported globally to date. This report describes the unique case of a 34-years-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis who developed concurrent aquaporin 4-immunoglobulin G-positive relapsing neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.

pmc-13275261.title: Assessment of Nutritional Risk Screening 2002 as predictors of long hospital stay in patients with upper gastrointestinal diseases
pmc-13275261.creator: Ruiqing Zhu, Xiao Li, Xiuxue Feng, Huikai Li, Fen Deng
pmc-13275261.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAmong patients admitted to the gastroenterology ward, especially those with upper gastrointestinal (UGI) diseases, malnutrition is markedly prevalent. Nutritional Risk Screening 2002 (NRS2002) is widely used globally to assess the nutritional risk of hospitalized patients.MethodsA retrospective, single-center study that included 896 patients with UGI diseases was performed in the Department of Esophagogastric‌, Senior Department of Gastroenterology, the First Medical Center of PLA General Hospital.

pmc-13623169.title: Advancing Occupational Noise-Induced Hearing Loss Risk Assessment in the Era of Large-Scale Data
pmc-13623169.creator: Wei Qiu, Michael Simpson
pmc-13623169.description: Occupational noise-induced hearing loss (NIHL) remains a leading occupational disorder worldwide and continues to impose substantial burdens on workers, employers, compensation systems, and health systems. ISO 1999 remains the principal framework for estimating population-level hearing loss associated with occupational noise exposure, while ISO 9612 provides the corresponding methodology for exposure determination.
